answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before submitting work, then slash bonds when random audits confirm fraud. A thousand sybils lock up a thousand stakes across the audit horizon; splitting capital does not create more. A low-bond haven lets honest newcomers enter, while rate limits constrain influence until work is verified. The attacker pays in tied-up capital and expected losses; the delta is that each fake identity adds cost, not free votes.
